**In short:**
The refund period for the Allottee in case of cancellation differs, with Document A stating a refund within ninety days [D14], while Document B specifies a refund within thirty days if the Allottee fails to execute and deliver the agreement [D45]. Regarding interest on refunds, Document A mentions interest at the rate specified in the Rules for refunds due to cancellation [D14], whereas Document B states that sums returned upon failure to execute the agreement shall be without any interest or compensation whatsoever [D45]. Both documents address the Promoter's obligation to pay interest for delays, but the specific timelines and conditions vary [D16][D35].

**Differences:**
* **Refunds/Cancellation:** If the Allottee cancels/withdraws without the promoter's fault, the promoter is entitled to forfeit ten percent of the total amount of the consideration money, interest and other dues payable for the allotment, and the balance amount shall be returned within ninety days [D14]. Conversely, if the Allottee fails to execute and deliver the agreement, the promoter shall return all sums deposited without any interest or compensation whatsoever if the default is not rectified within fifteen days of the notice [D45].
* **Interest on Delay/Refund:** If the Promoter fails to complete or give possession, the Promoter shall be liable to return the total amount received with interest at the rate specified in the Rules within ninety days, including compensation as provided under the Act [D15]. If the Promoter fails to abide by the time schedule, the Promoter agrees to pay interest as specified in the Rule on all amounts paid by the Allottee for every month of delay until possession is handed over [D35].
* **Payment Default/Termination:** If the Allottee fails to pay an installment, possession of the plot/apartment shall be extended to the extent of the period of delay in paying the defaulted amount, apart from paying interest on the delayed amount [D13]. If the Allottee commits three defaults of payment of installments, the Promoter may terminate the Agreement after giving fifteen days' notice, and the Promoter shall refund the installments paid within thirty days of termination, subject to adjustment for liquidated damages [D36].

**Only in Document A:**
* The Promoter must pay all outgoings collected from the Allottees before transferring physical possession, and if the Promoter fails to pay any outgoings, the Promoter remains liable to pay such outgoings and penal charges, and also liable for the cost of any legal proceedings taken by the authority [D10].
* If the Allottee fails to take possession after receiving written intimation, the Allottee shall continue to be liable to pay maintenance charges as applicable [D13].
* The Promoter must hand over necessary documents and plans, including common areas, to the association of the Allottees or the competent authority after obtaining the occupancy certificate [D13].
* The Promoter warrants that it has absolute, clear, and marketable title with respect to the said Land, requisite rights to carry out development, and absolute, actual, physical, and legal possession of the said Land for the Project [D17].

**Only in Document B:**
* The model form states that any clause found contrary to or inconsistent with any provisions of the Act, Rules and Regulations would be void ab-initio [D24].
* The Allottee shall use the Apartment only for the purpose of *residence/office/show-room/shop/godown for carrying on any industry or business* [D39].
* The Promoter shall transfer all the right, title, and interest of the Promoter/Vendor/Lessor/Original Owner to the society or Limited Company within three months of its registration [D40].
* The Allottee shall bear and pay the proportionate share of outgoings, such as local taxes, betterment charges, or water charges, within fifteen days of the Promoter's demand [D41].

**Which terms favour whom:**
* **Refund/Cancellation:** Document A provides a mechanism where the Promoter is liable to refund the total amount received with interest within ninety days if the Promoter fails to give possession for any reason, which is a broader liability than Document B's provisions [D15] vs [D38].
* **Binding Effect/Registration:** Document A requires the Allottee to sign, deliver, and appear for registration within thirty days, and failure to do so results in the return of sums without interest or compensation [D22]. Document B requires the Allottee to sign, deliver, and appear for registration within thirty days, but failure to do so results in the return of sums without interest or compensation, and the notice period for rectifying the default is fifteen days [D45].
